fields.features_heading: What a Chemical Peel Consent Form Holds
fields.features_subheading: Your provider writes the wording. The form presents it in short sections and files every signed visit on the client's record.
fields.feature_1:
Your wording, one section at a time

Paste the consent text your provider or lawyer approved. Each paragraph becomes its own section with an initials box, and the app shows the sentences exactly as written.
fields.feature_2:
Intake questions your provider chose

List the questions your provider asks before a peel, and each one becomes a required field. A yes answer appears at the top of that client's record, ahead of the signature.
fields.feature_3:
A signature with the name and date

The client signs with a finger or a mouse on the last screen. The app captures the e-signature with the client's name and the date, and saves it with the answers above it.
fields.feature_4:
One record for a series of peels

A client booked for 6 peels signs the full form at visit 1. Each later visit adds a dated confirmation to that same record. Staff open one page and see the whole series of peels.
fields.feature_5:
Emails that reach the right esthetician

Pick the answers that should reach a person, such as a client asking for a call. The app emails the esthetician on the booking, and the reply lands on the consent record.
fields.feature_6:
Signed forms in a table you own

Each submission is a row in a database you own, searchable by client, date, or location. Ask Emergent for a new column or a filter, and it changes the app from your prompt.

fields.usecase_heading: How Skin Clinics Use Peel Consent
fields.tab_content_1:
Before visit 3 of 6, Lenora answers 2 questions

Lenora Henrikson signs the full consent once, at visit 1 of a 6-peel series at Briarcliff Skin Studio. Before visit 3, her link opens 2 questions instead of the whole form: any changes since her last peel, and does she still agree to the signed terms. She signs, and her record reads visit 3 of 6 confirmed.
fields.tab_content_2:
Three locations share one form, and each sees its own list

Fernwell Med Spa sends one link for peel consent at all 3 of its locations, and the first question asks the client to pick Riverside, Northgate, or Elm Street. Gisela Brookhart manages Northgate. Her screen lists the 14 forms signed there this week, out of 41 across all 3 locations.
fields.tab_content_3:
When Nadira asks for a call on day 3, Faustine gets an email

Three days after her peel at Halcyon Aesthetics, Nadira Sefton gets a 3-question check-in email. She answers yes to a call from her esthetician. Faustine Delacey gets an email that says Nadira asked for a call, and the check-in answers save to Nadira's consent record.
fields.tab_content_4:
After each signature, the lobby tablet starts a blank form

A client who walks in unsigned at Celandine Skin Bar fills in the form on the lobby tablet before her peel. When she taps submit, the tablet clears her answers and opens a blank form for the next client. At the front desk, Zelda Corrigan sees 8 of 9 Saturday clients signed.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Chemical Peel Consent Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to an online chemical peel consent form your provider approved and clients sign before a peel.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Paste the form you use now
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Add the questions your provider asks
fields.howto_step_1_des: Paste the text of the form you use now into one prompt, or describe its sections if it only exists on paper. Name your clinic, the peels on your menu, and whether clients book a single peel or a series.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Send the consent wording to your provider or lawyer before any client sees it. Treat their version as final text: the form displays it, and it should not be rewritten to fit the screen.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Group the approved wording into sections a client can read on one phone screen each. Put the signature on the last screen, after the final section, and ask for initials on any section your provider names.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Type the questions your provider wants answered before a peel, and mark each one required. Choose which answers should email the esthetician on the booking.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Test it as a new client
fields.howto_step_5_des: Read the draft the way a first-time client would: open the form on a phone and fill it in as a new client, with no help from staff. Note every word you had to read twice, then ask Emergent to change it.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Tell Emergent where signed forms go: one table for every location, a visit count for a series, or a check-in email days after the peel. Each is a sentence in your prompt.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Publish the form and send the link
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the form and send its link with the booking confirmation, or open it on a lobby tablet. Building and publishing are covered by the free tier.

faq_plan.q: What is a chemical peel consent form?
faq_plan.a: A chemical peel consent form is the document a client reads and signs before a peel to record that she agrees to the treatment as your clinic describes it. For medical procedures, MedlinePlus describes written informed consent the same way: the patient reads a description of the treatment and signs a form. The description on your form comes from your provider, not from software.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a chemical peel consent form?
faq_plan.a: Describe the form in a prompt to Emergent's AI form builder: your clinic, the peels you offer, the questions your provider asks, and where signed forms should go. Emergent builds the form and the table that stores each response, and you change either by prompting again. Paste your provider's approved wording rather than asking for new text.

faq_plan.q: What should I change in a chemical peel consent form template before clients sign it?
faq_plan.a: Change the wording first. A chemical peel consent form template was written for another clinic, and your provider or lawyer should replace its text with theirs. Then match its list of peels to your menu and its questions to the ones your provider asks. Starting from a chemical peel consent form PDF works too: paste its text into the prompt and edit from there.

faq_plan.q: What makes a chemical peel consent form different from other service consents?
faq_plan.a: The shape is the same: approved wording, intake questions, and a signature. A tattoo consent form follows that pattern too. What differs is what surrounds the signature at a peel clinic, such as a series of visits on one record or a check-in a few days later. Build those into the form when your clinic runs them, and leave them out when it does not.

faq_plan.q: How do I show different wording on a chemical peel consent form for each type of peel?
faq_plan.a: Add a question near the top that asks which peel is booked, and show only the section your provider wrote for that peel. A client booked for one peel never scrolls past wording meant for another. Your provider decides how many versions exist and what each one says.

faq_plan.q: What should a chemical peel consent form do after a yes answer?
faq_plan.a: The answer should reach your provider before the peel starts, and your provider decides what happens next. Have the app email that answer to whoever performs the peel, and pin it to the top of the client's record. Leave the decision itself out of the form.

faq_plan.q: Can one visit cover a chemical peel consent form and another consent?
faq_plan.a: Yes: one link can open each treatment's consent in turn, each with its own wording and its own signature. A brow client who also books a peel could sign a permanent makeup consent form and the peel consent in one sitting. Each signature saves as a separate record with its treatment named on it.

faq_plan.q: How does a client get a copy of the chemical peel consent form she signed?
faq_plan.a: Email it to her the moment she submits. Ask Emergent to add a button on the confirmation screen that sends the client a copy of her answers and signature. The record in your table holds the same answers and signature as the copy she receives.

faq_plan.q: How do I update a chemical peel consent form when the wording changes?
faq_plan.a: Paste the new wording into a prompt, and Emergent changes the form. Ask it to save a version number with each signature. A record signed last spring then still shows the wording that client saw, and it stays in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can a chemical peel consent form live in the same app as my other service consents?
faq_plan.a: Yes: the app Emergent builds can hold a consent form for each service, all saving to client records in the same database. A spa that also waxes can add a waxing consent form next to the peel consent. Staff then open either one from the client's record.

plan.angle: The top 10 is downloadable chemical peel consent PDFs (ASCP's member sample, day spa and esthetician practice forms) plus one form-builder template: a sheet signed once and filed. This page shows what the clinic runs around the signature once the form is an app: a short re-confirmation on each visit of a peel series, one form shared by three locations with each location's own list, a day-3 check-in that lands on the consent record, and a lobby tablet that clears after every client. The consent wording stays with the clinic's provider or lawyer; the page makes no claim about peel risks, skin reactions, who may perform peels or whether a signature makes consent valid, and quotes MedlinePlus only for what written informed consent is.
